name: Merging PDF files
title: How to merge PDF files without installing anything
metaTitle: How to Merge PDF Files Free (2026 Guide)
metaDescription: Combine PDFs into one file for free. Drag to set the page order, mix in JPG and PNG images, keep bookmarks, and merge without Adobe Acrobat on Windows or Mac.
intro: Merging looks like the simplest thing you can do to a PDF, and it is the operation people get wrong most often: pages land in the wrong order, bookmarks vanish, a scanned receipt turns up sideways, and the output is somehow four times the size of the inputs. These guides cover ordering files properly, combining photos with documents, what a merge preserves and what it quietly destroys, and how to do all of it without a subscription.
answer: Add every PDF to a merge tool, drag the files into the order you want, then merge and download one combined file. Pages keep their internal order within each file, so the file list decides everything. A browser-based merge runs locally, so nothing is uploaded to a server.

posts.title: How to merge PDF files for free
posts.metaTitle: How to Merge PDF Files for Free
posts.metaDescription: Merge two or more PDFs into one file in your browser. Drag to set the page order, keep bookmarks and links intact, and check the result before downloading.
posts.answer: Open a browser merge tool, add every PDF you want to combine, drag the files into the order you need, then click Merge and download the single output file. Order is decided by the file list, top to bottom, and pages inside each file keep their own order.

body.x: Merging is a structural operation, not a rendering one. A well-built merge tool copies each page object from the source files into a new document and rebuilds the page tree. Nothing is re-drawn, re-compressed or re-typeset, so the text stays crisp and the file size is roughly the sum of the inputs.
The five-step version

items.x: Go to [merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf). The files are processed in your browser, so nothing leaves your computer and there is no size cap imposed by an upload.
Drag the whole selection in together rather than one at a time. In Finder or File Explorer, click the first file, then Shift-click the last to select a run.

Drag the file cards into position. The first card becomes page 1. Check the page count shown on each card against what you expected, which catches the wrong-version-of-the-file mistake before it becomes a 60-page problem.
The combined document is built locally. A 12-file, 200-page merge finishes in a couple of seconds on a normal laptop.

items.h: Check page 1 and the last page
items.x: Open the result in a [PDF reader](/tools/pdf-reader) and confirm the first and last pages are what you expect. Those two checks catch almost every ordering error.

body.x: Combine any number of PDFs into one document, entirely in your browser.
Getting the order right the first time

Most merge mistakes are ordering mistakes, and they happen because operating systems sort filenames as text, not as numbers. `chapter10.pdf` sorts before `chapter2.pdf` because the character "1" comes before "2".

Zero-pad the numbers and the problem disappears permanently: `01-cover.pdf`, `02-summary.pdf`, `10-appendix.pdf`. Once the filenames sort correctly, dragging the whole batch in gives you the right order with no manual reordering at all.

For a scanned double-sided batch, scan all the odd pages, then all the even pages, and use a merge tool that supports alternate-page interleaving. Without it you get every front page followed by every back page, which is the single most common scanning complaint.
What survives a merge, and what does not

body.caption: PDF features and how they behave when files are combined.
head: Feature
After merging
What to do about it
rows: Nothing. Fonts are copied, subsets get merged.
Internal links within one source file
Check any table of contents links.
Better tools nest each file under a parent bookmark; simple ones drop them.
Rename fields first, or flatten the forms before merging.
Merge first, then sign the combined document.
A merged file can legitimately mix A4 and Letter pages.
Taken from the first file, or blank
Set the title and author afterwards.

body.x: A merge invalidates every existing digital signature in the source files, because signing covers the byte range of the document it was applied to and merging rewrites that. Always merge before you [sign](/tools/sign-pdf), never after.
Mixed page sizes

PDF stores a page size per page, so a merged document can contain A4 (210 × 297 mm), US Letter (216 × 279 mm) and a stray landscape spreadsheet page without any conflict. On screen this is invisible. On paper it is obvious: pages alternate between slightly taller and slightly wider, and a printer set to A4 will scale the Letter pages by about 96 percent.

If the document will be printed, normalise the page size before merging: re-export the odd file from its source application at the size you want, or print each file to PDF with a fixed paper size selected. If the document will only be read on screen, leave it alone.
Why the merged file is bigger than expected
The output is normally close to the sum of the inputs, plus a little. Three things inflate it further:

items: **Duplicated fonts.** Each source file carries its own embedded font subsets. Ten reports built from the same template can end up with ten copies of the same typeface, adding several megabytes.
**Scanned pages.** A 300 DPI colour scan is roughly 1 to 3 MB per page before compression. Twenty scanned pages will dominate a merge regardless of what else is in it.
**Images stored at full camera resolution.** A 12-megapixel photo placed on a page is still 12 megapixels inside the PDF, even though it displays at postcard size.

body.x: Compression fixes all three: it de-duplicates identical objects, downsamples images to a sensible DPI, and re-encodes scans. A 60 MB merged batch of scans usually lands between 5 and 12 MB with no visible change on screen. See [reducing PDF file size for email](/blog/compress/reduce-pdf-file-size-for-email).
Merged file too big to send? Compress it before you attach it.
When merging fails

head: Symptom
Cause
Fix
rows: Tool refuses one of the files
Open it, enter the password, and re-save an unprotected copy
The file is truncated or malformed
The source page carries a rotation flag
Text looks different in one section
A font was not embedded in that source file
Re-export that file with fonts embedded
A file contains hundreds of high-resolution images
Compress that file first, then merge

body.x: After the merge

A combined document usually needs two finishing touches. First, [page numbers](/tools/page-numbers), because the original per-file numbering no longer makes sense across a 90-page compilation. Second, a set of bookmarks so a reader can jump between the original documents. If the merged file is going outside your organisation, also check what the [metadata](/tools/edit-metadata) says: it inherits the author name from whichever file was first in the list.

faqs.q: How do I merge PDF files without uploading them anywhere?
faqs.a: Use a merge tool that runs in the browser using WebAssembly rather than a server. The files are read by JavaScript on your own machine, combined locally, and offered back as a download. Nothing is transmitted, which also means there is no upload size limit.

faqs.q: Can I merge PDFs on Windows without extra software?
faqs.a: No. Windows 10 and 11 have no built-in PDF merge. Microsoft Print to PDF is a virtual printer that can only handle one document at a time, and Edge can view PDFs but not combine them. You need either a browser tool or an installed application.

faqs.q: Does merging reduce the quality of a PDF?
faqs.a: No. A proper merge copies page objects without re-rendering anything, so text, vectors and images are byte-identical to the originals. Quality only changes if you also compress the result.

faqs.q: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
faqs.a: A browser tool is limited by available memory rather than a fixed count. Fifty text documents merge without trouble; fifty large scanned files may need to be done in two passes on a machine with less RAM.

faqs.q: Will merging keep the bookmarks from each file?
faqs.a: It depends on the tool. Better implementations create a parent bookmark per source file and nest the original outline underneath. Simpler ones drop the outline entirely, in which case you can add bookmarks to the merged document afterwards.

posts.title: How to combine PDFs without Adobe Acrobat
posts.metaDescription: Merge PDFs without paying for Acrobat. macOS Preview step by step, why Windows 11 cannot do it, what Google Drive really offers, and free browser tools.
posts.answer: macOS can merge PDFs for free in Preview: open one file, show Thumbnails, drag the second PDF into the sidebar, then use File, Export as PDF. Windows 11 has no built-in merge and Google Drive cannot combine files either, so on those platforms use a free browser-based merge tool.

body.x: Acrobat Pro is the reference implementation and it costs roughly the price of a streaming subscription every month, billed annually. If merging is the only thing you need, you are paying for a page editor, a form designer, a redaction engine and a PDF printer you will not use. Here is what each free route actually does.
macOS: Preview does merge, with one trap
Preview is a real PDF editor pretending to be a viewer. It has merged PDFs since Mac OS X 10.6 and there is nothing to install.

items.h: Open the first PDF in Preview
items.x: Double-click it, or right-click and choose Open With → Preview if another app has claimed the file type.
Press **⌥⌘2**, or use **View → Thumbnails**. Nothing else works without it.

items.h: Drag the second PDF into the sidebar
items.x: Drag from Finder and drop it **between two thumbnails**, so a horizontal insertion line appears. Do not drop it on top of a thumbnail.
Drag thumbnails up and down. Select several with ⌘-click or Shift-click and move them as a group.
Use **File → Export as PDF**. Saving in place can leave the second document embedded as an annotation rather than flattened into the page tree.

body.x: The trap is step 3. Dropping a PDF **onto** a page thumbnail attaches it as an annotation instead of inserting its pages. The file looks merged in Preview and arrives as a single page with a paperclip icon for everyone else. If your merged file is suspiciously small, this is what happened.
Windows: there is no built-in way, and that surprises people
Windows 11 ships a PDF viewer inside Edge and a virtual printer called Microsoft Print to PDF. Neither can combine two files.

body.caption: What Windows tools can and cannot do with PDFs.
head: Tool
View
Print to PDF
Merge two PDFs
rows: Yes, one document at a time
Opens and converts, reflowing the layout
Only by inserting each PDF as an object, which rasterises it

body.x: The Word route deserves a specific warning. **Insert → Object → Text from File** will place a PDF in a Word document, but Word converts each page to a picture and often only imports the first page. The output is a document of images: unsearchable, large, and unprintable at any real quality. It is not a merge.
Google Drive cannot merge PDFs either

This one costs people the most time, because it feels like it should work. Drive stores PDFs, previews them, and can OCR one into a Google Doc. It has no combine function. Opening two PDFs as Docs and pasting one into the other destroys the layout entirely, since the conversion turns a fixed-layout document into a reflowing one. Third-party Workspace add-ons exist, but they upload your files to that vendor, which is usually the opposite of what someone choosing Drive for privacy reasons wanted.
Browser tools: the answer on Windows, and fine everywhere

A merge tool built on WebAssembly does the work inside the page, on your own machine. The distinction matters: an "online PDF merger" usually means your document is uploaded to someone else's server, processed there, and deleted on a promise. A browser-based tool never sends the bytes anywhere.

items: Open [merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf) and drop the files in.
Drag them into order and merge.
Download the result. No account, no watermark, no page limit.

body.x: Merge PDFs on Windows, Mac, Linux or ChromeOS, with no upload and no install.
Command line, if you already live there

Three tools do this well and all are free. **qpdf** is the most correct: it preserves structure and is actively maintained. **pdftk** is the classic and still fine for simple jobs. **Ghostscript** re-writes the file, which can shrink it but also re-encodes images.

# qpdf, cleanest structural merge
qpdf --empty --pages a.pdf b.pdf c.pdf -- merged.pdf

# qpdf, merge only pages 1-3 of a.pdf with all of b.pdf
qpdf --empty --pages a.pdf 1-3 b.pdf -- merged.pdf

# pdftk, the classic
pdftk a.pdf b.pdf cat output merged.pdf

# Ghostscript, re-writes and often compresses
gs -dBATCH -dNOPAUSE -q -sDEVICE=pdfwrite \
   -sOutputFile=merged.pdf a.pdf b.pdf

On macOS there is also a hidden Automator action at `/System/Library/Automator/Combine PDF Pages.action`, and a Python script Apple ships with Preview's print pipeline. Both work, and both are more effort than dragging thumbnails.
Choosing between them

head: Situation
Best option
rows: Mac, two or three files, one-off
Browser tool that runs locally, or qpdf offline
qpdf or pdftk in a script
Command line, driven by a loop
You need bookmarks nested per source file
qpdf, or a tool that advertises outline preservation

body.x: What you give up by not buying Acrobat

Honestly, not much for merging. Where Acrobat still earns its price is true redaction that removes the underlying text rather than covering it, PDF/A validation and conversion, accessibility tagging for screen readers, and Bates numbering for legal discovery. Combining files is not on that list. Neither is [reordering pages](/blog/merge/reorder-pdf-pages), [splitting](/blog/split/split-pdf-into-pages) or compression, all of which have solid free equivalents.

faqs.q: Can Windows 11 merge PDF files without software?
faqs.a: No. There is no built-in merge in Windows 10 or 11. Microsoft Print to PDF handles one document at a time and Edge can only view and annotate. A browser-based merge tool is the closest thing to a built-in option.

faqs.q: How do I merge PDFs on a Mac for free?
faqs.a: Open the first PDF in Preview, press Option+Command+2 to show thumbnails, drag the second PDF into the sidebar between two page thumbnails, then choose File then Export as PDF. Do not drop the file on top of a thumbnail or it becomes an attachment.

faqs.q: Can Google Drive combine two PDFs?
faqs.a: No. Drive can store, preview and OCR PDFs but has no merge function. Converting them to Google Docs and pasting one into the other destroys the fixed layout, so it is not a workaround.

faqs.q: Is a free PDF merger safe for confidential documents?
faqs.a: Only if it processes files in your browser rather than uploading them. Check whether the tool describes local or client-side processing. If a file has to be uploaded to be merged, treat the document as having left your control.

faqs.q: Does Adobe Acrobat Reader merge PDFs?
faqs.a: The free Reader does not. Merging is a paid Acrobat feature, and Adobe also offers a limited web version that requires signing in and caps free use.

posts.title: How to add scanned images to an existing PDF
posts.metaTitle: Add Scanned Images to an Existing PDF
posts.metaDescription: Convert supported images into PDF pages, then merge them with an existing document. Set page size, check rotation and review the final order before sharing.
posts.primaryKeyword: add images to an existing pdf
secondaryKeywords: scan multiple pages to one pdf
posts.answer: Convert JPG, PNG or WebP images to PDF pages first, then merge that PDF with your existing PDFs. The JPG to PDF tool does not accept HEIC directly, so convert HEIC to JPG first. Once each input is a PDF, arrange the files and download one combined document.

body.x: PDF pages hold images perfectly well, but a merge tool works on PDFs, not on a mixed pile of formats. The reliable pattern is two steps: normalise everything to PDF, then combine. Doing it in that order also gives you a chance to fix orientation and page size before anything is locked into a page tree.
Step 1: turn the images into PDF pages

items.h: Gather the images in one folder
items.x: Rename them so they sort in the order you want: `01.jpg`, `02.jpg`, and so on. Zero-padding matters, because `10.jpg` sorts before `2.jpg` otherwise.
Go to [JPG to PDF](/tools/jpg-to-pdf) and drop the whole folder selection in at once.

Under Page size, choose **A4**, **Letter** or **Same as image**. Then choose **Fit inside margins**, **Fill page** or **Original size**. Fit inside margins keeps the whole picture visible; Fill page can crop its edges.

The converter does not offer an EXIF auto-rotate switch. Open the output and check each page; if one is sideways, rotate it with [Organize Pages](/tools/organize-pdf) or [Rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf).
You get either one PDF per image or a single multi-page PDF, depending on the option chosen. For merging, one multi-page PDF is fewer things to drag.

body.x: Convert JPG, PNG and WebP images into PDF pages in your browser. Convert HEIC to JPG first.
HEIC: why iPhone photos need a moment

The JPG to PDF tool accepts JPG, PNG and WebP, not HEIC. Convert HEIC images with [HEIC to JPG](/tools/heic-to-jpg) first, then add the resulting JPG files. The conversion changes the image format, so check the converted file before assembling a document.

If you would rather avoid the issue entirely, change the camera setting: **Settings → Camera → Formats → Most Compatible** makes the iPhone shoot JPEG instead. And if you AirDrop photos to a Mac, macOS converts on the fly, which is why the same photo is sometimes HEIC and sometimes JPEG depending on how it arrived.
Step 2: merge everything

With every input now a PDF, open [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf), add the files in the intended sequence, check the order shown, and run the merge. A typical expense claim might contain a cover letter, receipt pages and a statement. Review the output before sending it.
Getting the resolution right

This is where image-to-PDF goes wrong. An image has pixels; a PDF page has physical dimensions. The relationship between them is DPI, and choosing badly gives you either a blurry printout or a 90 MB file.

body.caption: Pixels needed to fill a full page at common resolutions.
head: Page
At 150 DPI (screen, draft print)
At 300 DPI (proper print)
At 600 DPI (archival scan)
rows: 4032 × 3024 px, more than enough for any of these

body.x: Image pixel dimensions affect how sharp a page looks when printed. The JPG to PDF tool does not provide a DPI or image-resampling setting, so prepare a smaller copy in an image editor if you need to reduce resolution before conversion. Keep the original, and inspect a test page at the intended print size.
The receipt problem, worked through

The output size depends on the number and dimensions of the source images. Email and workplace upload limits vary, so check the current limit for the account or portal you are using. If the PDF is too large, make a backup and try the options below:

items: Resize or convert copies of the source photos in an image editor before making the PDF. This JPG to PDF tool does not offer a DPI or grayscale option, so check that small receipt text remains readable.
Use the browser's print or image tools only if their output is suitable; compare the result with the original before discarding anything.
Try [Compress PDF](/tools/compress-pdf) on a copy. Medium and Strong turn pages into images, which can reduce size but removes selectable text and may lower detail.

body.x: Photograph receipts against a dark surface in even light and crop tightly before converting. A tight crop with high contrast both shrinks the file and dramatically improves OCR accuracy later.
Making the result searchable

A PDF made from photos contains no text, only pictures of text. Ctrl+F finds nothing, and neither will your accounting software or your operating system search index. Running [OCR](/tools/ocr-pdf) adds an invisible text layer under the image: the page looks identical, but the amounts, dates and vendor names become searchable and copyable. For a receipts archive this is the difference between a folder you use and a folder you forget.
Add a searchable text layer to a PDF built from photos or scans.

body.caption: Common jobs and the order to do them in.
head: Job
Sequence
rows: Check/crop copies → JPG to PDF → merge → OCR if searchable text is needed → compare compression on a copy
Signed contract, scan mixed with the original
Scan signature pages → images to PDF → merge with the original → do not compress
PNG to PDF, fit to image, full resolution → merge → do not compress
Passport and ID for an application
Photos to PDF at Letter or A4 → merge → check nothing is cropped at the edges
A book or manual you photographed
Images to PDF → merge → OCR → add [page numbers](/tools/page-numbers)

body.x: A note on quality loss

Placing a JPEG into a PDF is lossless: the original JPEG bytes are embedded as-is, so the page is exactly as good as the file you started with. Quality is only lost if you downsample during conversion or compress afterwards, both of which are choices you control. PNG behaves differently, since PDF re-encodes it, but the result is still visually identical for screenshots and diagrams.

faqs.q: How do I combine photos and a PDF into one file?
faqs.a: Convert the photos into PDF pages first with an image-to-PDF tool, then merge the resulting PDF with your existing one. Merge tools only accept PDFs, so the conversion step is what makes the combination possible.

faqs.q: Can I merge HEIC photos from my iPhone into a PDF?
faqs.a: Not directly with PrintxPDF's JPG to PDF tool, which accepts JPG, PNG and WebP. Convert HEIC to JPG with [HEIC to JPG](/tools/heic-to-jpg), then create PDF pages and merge them. On iPhone, Most Compatible camera format saves future photos as JPEG.

faqs.q: What resolution should I use for images in a PDF?
faqs.a: Use 150 DPI for documents that will only be read on screen and 300 DPI for anything that will be printed. For US Letter that means 1275 by 1650 pixels and 2550 by 3300 pixels respectively. Higher adds size without adding visible detail.

faqs.q: Why is my photo sideways in the PDF?
faqs.a: The JPG to PDF tool does not expose an EXIF auto-rotate setting. Check the output and rotate a sideways page with [Organize Pages](/tools/organize-pdf) or [Rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf).

faqs.q: How do I scan several pages into a single PDF?
faqs.a: Most scanner software has a multi-page or batch mode that outputs one PDF. If yours produces one file per page, convert or collect them and merge the results, which also lets you drop the blank reverse sides.

posts.title: How to reorder, rotate and delete PDF pages
posts.metaTitle: Reorder, Rotate and Delete PDF Pages
posts.metaDescription: Fix a PDF whose pages are out of order, sideways or unwanted. Drag thumbnails to reorder, rotate in 90 degree steps, remove pages and save the result.
posts.answer: Open the PDF in a page organiser, drag the page thumbnails into the order you want, use the rotate buttons for any sideways page, select unwanted pages and delete them, then download. Rotation is stored as a page property, so a rotated page stays rotated in every viewer and on paper.

body.x: Three operations, one interface. Reordering, rotating and deleting all edit the same thing: the page tree that tells a PDF reader which pages exist and in what sequence. That is why every decent tool puts them on one screen full of thumbnails rather than in three separate menus.
The workflow

items.h: Open the file in a page organiser
items.x: Go to [organize PDF](/tools/organize-pdf) and drop the file in. Every page appears as a thumbnail with its page number.
Drag a thumbnail to a new position. Select a run with Shift-click, or scattered pages with Ctrl-click (⌘-click on macOS), then move them as a block.
Hover a page and use the rotate buttons. Rotation goes in 90 degree steps only, because that is all the PDF format stores. Select several pages to rotate them together.

items.h: Delete what you do not need
items.x: Select the pages and press Delete, or type a range such as `2,5,11-13` if the tool accepts one.
Open the result and check the page count. If you deleted four pages from a 40-page file, the output must be 36 pages.

body.x: Reorder, rotate and delete pages on one screen, without uploading the file.
Why your rotation did not stick

PDF stores rotation as a **`/Rotate`** entry on each page, and it accepts exactly four values: 0, 90, 180 and 270. Many PDF readers offer a View → Rotate command that turns the page on screen without touching that entry. Close the file and the rotation is gone, because nothing was written. To make it permanent you need a tool that edits the page object and saves a new file, which is what a page organiser or [rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf) does.

This is also why a page can look upright in one app and sideways in another. If the rotation lives only in a viewer's display state, every other viewer starts from the stored value. Write it into the file and the ambiguity disappears.
The double-sided scan problem

A single-sided document feeder gives you a very specific mess. You scan all the fronts, flip the stack, scan all the backs, and end up with pages 1, 3, 5, 7 followed by 8, 6, 4, 2. Reversed, because flipping the stack reverses the order of the reverse sides.

items: Reverse the second batch so the even pages run 2, 4, 6, 8.
Interleave the two batches, taking one page from each in turn. Some merge tools call this **alternate and mix**.
Delete the blank backs, which is usually most of them.
Rotate any page the feeder pulled in sideways.

body.x: Blank scanned pages are rarely truly blank: dust and paper texture leave speckles, so a "delete blank pages" filter that looks for pure white will miss them. Sorting by page byte size is a better heuristic, since a genuinely empty scan is a fraction of the size of one with text on it.
What breaks when you move pages around

items: **Bookmarks point at page objects, not page numbers.** Reordering usually keeps them working; deleting a bookmarked page leaves a dead entry that jumps nowhere.

**Printed page numbers do not update.** The number drawn on the page is part of the page content. After reordering, either accept the mismatch or strip and re-apply them with [page numbers](/tools/page-numbers).
**Cross-references inside the text go stale.** "See page 14" is just text.
**Digital signatures are invalidated.** Any structural edit breaks a signature. Reorganise first, sign last.
**Form field tab order** follows the original page sequence in some documents and needs to be reset.

body.x: Deleting is not redacting

Removing a page removes it from the page tree. Depending on how the file is written, the underlying objects can survive in the file as orphaned data, particularly if the editor saves an incremental update rather than rewriting the whole document. For confidential material, use a tool that fully rewrites the file, then [flatten](/tools/flatten-pdf) it and [strip the metadata](/tools/remove-metadata). More on that in [deleting pages from a PDF](/blog/split/delete-pages-from-pdf).
Just need to turn a few pages the right way up and save it properly?
A sensible order of operations

When a document needs several fixes, do them in this order: merge everything first, then reorder, then rotate, then delete, then add page numbers, then OCR if it is scanned, and compress last. Compression goes last because every earlier step rewrites the file and would undo it. Signing, if needed, goes after compression, because signing must be the final change.

faqs.q: How do I permanently rotate a page in a PDF?
faqs.a: Use a tool that edits the page and saves a new file rather than a viewer that only rotates the display. The rotation is stored as a /Rotate value of 0, 90, 180 or 270 on the page itself, which is what makes it persist across viewers and when printing.

faqs.q: How do I rearrange PDF pages on a Mac?
faqs.a: Open the PDF in Preview, press Option+Command+2 to show thumbnails, then drag pages into the order you want. Use File then Export as PDF to save a clean copy rather than saving in place.

faqs.q: Can I reorder PDF pages without Adobe Acrobat?
faqs.a: Yes. macOS Preview does it for free, and browser-based page organisers work on Windows, Linux and ChromeOS with no installation. Acrobat is not required for any page-level operation.

faqs.q: My scanned document has every second page upside down. How do I fix it?
faqs.a: The feeder scanned the reverse sides while the paper was inverted. Select just the even-numbered pages in a page organiser and rotate that selection 180 degrees in one action, rather than fixing them one at a time.

faqs.q: Does reordering pages change the file size?
faqs.a: Barely. Reordering rewrites the page tree, which is a small part of the file, while the page content stays as it was. Deleting pages does reduce the size, roughly in proportion to what those pages contained.

posts.title: How to combine PDF files in a custom page order
posts.metaTitle: Combine PDFs and Put Pages in the Right Order
posts.metaDescription: Build one PDF packet from several files, rearrange pages, remove extras and check the final order before you share or print it.
posts.primaryKeyword: combine pdf files custom page order
posts.answer: To combine PDFs in a custom order, list the files in the sequence you want, merge them, then inspect the page thumbnails and move, rotate, extract or delete pages as needed. Save a new copy, check page count and orientation, and open the output before sending it. Keep the originals until the packet is verified.

body.x: A packet assembled from separate scans or forms often needs more than a merge. A cover may belong first, a signature page last, and one blank scan may need to go. Plan the sequence before editing, then check it page by page. The tools below work locally in your browser, so the PDFs are not uploaded.
Plan the order before you combine files

Rename copies with simple prefixes such as 01-cover, 02-form and 03-attachment, or write the intended order on a checklist. Filenames help you keep track, but do not prove that the contents are correct. Open each source and identify its page count, orientation and any password or digital signature that could be affected by saving a new file.

items.x: Open [Merge PDF](/tools/merge-pdf), add the files and arrange the file order before running the merge. The first input starts the output unless you move it.
Check thumbnails and scroll through the output, not only the first and last pages. Look for duplicated covers, reversed scans, blank pages and landscape pages mixed into a portrait packet.
For page-level changes, use [Organize Pages](/tools/organize-pdf) and drag pages into the intended order. Rotate sideways scans with [Rotate PDF](/tools/rotate-pdf).

Use [Delete Pages](/tools/delete-pages) for unwanted pages, [Extract Pages](/tools/extract-pages) to keep a selected range in a separate file, or [Split PDF](/tools/split-pdf) to divide the packet into groups.

items.h: Save and verify a new copy
items.x: Confirm the page count and order, then open the final PDF in a reader. Keep original files until the recipient has the right document and your retention policy allows cleanup.

body.x: Combine several PDFs in the sequence you choose, then verify the result.
Merge, organize, extract or split?

head: Need
Use
Result
rows: One file with all pages in input order.
One file with the same pages in a new order.
A new PDF containing the chosen pages.
Remove pages from the source copy
A new PDF without the specified pages.
Several outputs based on page ranges or split settings.
